legend: You are given a tree where vertices are labeled with integers 1,2,…,N%%ZSMJ0%%.

For a subset of vertices S⊆{1,2,…,N}%%ZSMJ1%%, we say two vertices (u,v)%%ZSMJ2%% are connected under S%%ZSMJ3%% if there exists a path that only passes through the vertices in S%%ZSMJ4%%. Note that this includes endpoints of the path, so u,v∈S%%ZSMJ5%% should hold.
For example, consider the following tree and the set S={1,2,3,4,5,6}%%ZSMJ6%%.
In this case, (1,2)%%ZSMJ7%%, (3,5)%%ZSMJ8%% and (4,6)%%ZSMJ9%% are connected under S%%ZSMJ10%%, while (1,6)%%ZSMJ11%% and (2,7)%%ZSMJ12%% are not connected under S%%ZSMJ13%%.

Let strength(S)%%ZSMJ14%% be the number of pairs of vertices (u,v)%%ZSMJ15%% such that u≠v%%ZSMJ16%% and (u,v)%%ZSMJ17%% are connected under S%%ZSMJ18%%. You are given Q%%ZSMJ19%% queries, where each query contains a set S%%ZSMJ20%%. For each query, you should compute the quantity strength(S)%%ZSMJ21%%.
input: The first line contains a single integer N%%ZSMJ22%%, the number of vertices (2≤N≤250000%%ZSMJ23%%).
Each of the next N−1%%ZSMJ24%% lines contains two space-separated integers a%%ZSMJ25%% and b%%ZSMJ26%%: the vertices connected by an edge (1≤a,b≤N%%ZSMJ27%%). Together, the edges form a tree.
The next line contains a single integer Q%%ZSMJ28%%, the number of queries (1≤Q≤100000%%ZSMJ29%%).

Each of the next Q%%ZSMJ30%% lines contains a query, denoted by space-separated integers. A query starts with an integer K%%ZSMJ31%%, the size of the set (1≤K≤N%%ZSMJ32%%). It is followed by K%%ZSMJ33%% distinct integers from 1%%ZSMJ34%% to N%%ZSMJ35%% in arbitrary order: the vertices of set S%%ZSMJ36%%.
The sum of K%%ZSMJ37%% in each test case is at most 1000000%%ZSMJ38%%.
output: For each of the Q%%ZSMJ39%% queries, print a single line with the integer strength(S)%%ZSMJ40%% as defined above.
